title: Glass harmonica
summary: The glass harmonica is a row of glass bowls of falling sizes nested on one spindle that turns on a pedal. A player touches the wet rims, and each bowl sings with its own soft, pure note.
howToPlay: Ten bowls are lit, from the largest and lowest on the left to the smallest and highest on the right.
Play the bowl a closing ring marks. Its rim glows as it sings.
The tone swells slowly. Start each note early and let it sound.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: A coloured band on each rim tells the note, so a player can find the bowl at a glance. The turning bowls dip in water to keep the glass wet.
credits: Tradition: the glass harmonica; patterns written for this game
